doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: No lines between music or between people; Tribal Disorder Productions
summary: He sees genre boundaries as artificial like the divisions between people, describes his travels and his company Tribal Disorder Productions, and lists his range from Cab Calloway to the chitlin circuit.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Um hum. Well I’m struck by the length and the breadth of your experience, from Sun Ra to Shostakovich, and I don’t have a question here but it’s simply an observation that you don’t compartmentalize music, I guess, that’s my guess.

Yeah I think these lines that are placed between this and between that and all these things, these are artificial lines that people have placed. And that’s symbolic of the lines that we human beings place between each other in life, all over the world in all kinds of ways we have all of these lines that say I’m different from you. And that’s the biggest bunch of bullshit going in the world. You know this is what’s keeping us at war. This is what’s keeping us with all of this strife is that we make these lines instead of saying hey wait a minute, we don’t have to be that way. You know I’ve been blessed to be able to travel over a great part of the world. And I get to travel in a way so that I’m in places for

a while. I get to know people who live in places. And people are people when it comes down to it. And then we’re saying, “Oh yeah but I don’t like them because they’re like this and –” it’s crazy. I know of people in Paris where you have Iranian and Israeli making music together. Now this is an example of how we humans need to learn how to live. My production company is Tribal Disorder Productions. We’re a force against the disorder in the human tribe. I know humanity is a species, not a tribe, but I’m using tribe to say hey, it’s time for us to come together as one tribe. And we are, I think, at an existential state right now as far as where we are as humans getting along. Sun Ra always said that harmony, musicians are here to make harmony among people, to bring people together. And that’s what my life has been. Yeah. Like you said, Shostakovich to Sun Ra to Archie Shepp to, I came up in Cab Calloway’s band and playing shows and stuff, Broadway shows. So all of that, and really, before that I played the chitlin circuit playing R&B where that was really crazy, playing in places where they’re bootlegging the liquor you know.
